summary: GMDSS batteries and chargers, and how linear and switching power supplies turn ship's power into steady DC.

blocks.title: Cells and batteries
items: A cell is 2 materials in an electrolyte. Its chemistry sets its voltage.
Series: voltages add, and the same current flows through every cell.

blocks.title: Checking a lead acid cell
items: Specific gravity: how heavy the electrolyte is compared with water. Full cell 1.280, discharged around 1.12. Measure it with a hydrometer.
Warmer electrolyte expands and reads lower. The charge hasn't changed.
Reverse polarity: a weak cell runs out first, and the other cells' discharge current charges it in reverse.
Gel cell: typically sealed. Special charging rates and voltages may be required.

blocks.title: Reserve power and charging
items: Reserve Source of Energy: power to operate the radio installation and conduct Distress and Safety communications if main and emergency power fail.
Charge rates: high (Full) refills fast, float holds full, trickle makes up self-discharge.
Weekly high charge (standard lead acid): until the gassing range, where water splits into gas. Weak cells catch up.
The charger then interrupts it to inhibit electrolytic gas.
Maintenance free lead acid gel: high (Full) mode disabled during setup.

blocks.title: Rectifiers
items: Half wave: 1 diode. Full wave: 2 diodes with a center tap, or a bridge of 4 with none.
Ripple: in a full wave supply, twice the input frequency.

blocks.title: Switching supplies
items: Advantages: line voltage directly rectified and filtered to high DC; much smaller, lighter parts; much better efficiency. Also wide input range, DC input.
Disadvantages: increased complexity, increased cost, radiated RF.
Ferrite core: reduces losses at high frequencies.
Duty cycle: the share of each period the switch is on.
Crowbar: prevents overvoltage damage by shorting the output.
Input current: short pulses near the AC peaks: high harmonic content, low power factor.

blocks.title: Exam traps
items: NICAD isn't 1.5 V. 2.5 V isn't a cell voltage.
Use a hydrometer, not a voltmeter. 1.210 and 1.180 aren't full.
Float, trickle, Full and boost are rates, not charger modes.
High charge stops for gas, not heat.
No RFI problems is no switcher advantage. It's radiated RF, not AF.
Switcher core: not laminated steel.
Feedback runs to the controller, not the input.
